conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you came in because your dialysis access wasn't working?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I couldn't get dialysis today. My arm felt fine, but they said no blood flow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You also mentioned painful bumps on your abdomen where you inject insulin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they've been getting bigger for three weeks. I finished antibiotics but no improvement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And you've had burning when you urinate and cloudy, smelly urine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, for about three weeks. I finished another antibiotic but still feel the same.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We'll check your arm, abdomen, and urine. You're not running a fever, but we'll start antibiotics just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thank you. I'm worried about my dialysis access failing again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We'll get imaging on your arm tomorrow to see what's going on. For now, rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your CT scan shows your bladder wall is inflamed, likely infection. The abdominal bumps aren't abscesses.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it's not calciphylaxis again? I couldn't tolerate that treatment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No calcium deposits were seen. We'll watch them as possible panniculitis. No treatment change now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That's a relief. What about my arm?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You have a clot in your AV graft. You'll have a procedure today to clear it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it work? I've had clots before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The radiologist is experienced. They'll use medication and tools to open it. Success is likely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The procedure was successful. The clot is gone, and blood is flowing through your graft.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you! Can I do dialysis tomorrow?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, scheduled for tomorrow. We'll also check your breast wound.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It's been oozing a little. Is it infected?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We took a sample. It grew E. coli and Proteus, both sensitive to the antibiotic we're giving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Like last time? That was painful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Different bacteria, but we're treating it effectively. Ultrasound shows no abscess.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. What about my urine infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The culture was contaminated, so we can't confirm. But your symptoms are improving with antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You completed dialysis yesterday. Your labs are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel better. When can I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We want to finish your IV antibiotics. You'll get them during dialysis sessions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I'll go home and come back for antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the antibiotic will be given after each dialysis. We'll switch to oral if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my wound care?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Wound care team recommends daily dressing changes with saline and special packing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can do that at home with help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and follow up with your wound nurse practitioner.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your white count is down, creatinine improving. You're healing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Any news on the back spot from the CT?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The lytic spot in your spine is likely benign, maybe a Schmorl's node. MRI can clarify if needed later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I'd rather not unless it's urgent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Agreed. We'll monitor. Your blood pressure is stable on your meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're doing well. We'll plan discharge tomorrow if labs stay stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I'm ready to go home. Will I need rehab?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Physical therapy says you can go home with support. We'll arrange services.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final labs look good. Your infection markers are down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You'll get ceftazidime after each dialysis for now. Repeat urine culture if symptoms return.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my abdominal bumps?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Follow up with dermatology if they change. No treatment now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're cleared to go home. Take your meds, do wound care, and attend dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for fixing my access and treating the infections.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're welcome. Call if you develop fever, chest pain, or trouble breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And check labs in a week?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and follow up with nephrology and your primary team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Glad to hear it. You handled everything well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again, doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We'll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I'll make sure to keep all my appointments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That's the best way to stay healthy. Safe travels home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Appreciate it. Have a good day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You too. Call us with any concerns.
